name: fin71-2
why: Gemma's parting slip is a terrific moment, but the long, repetitive second day makes the outcome feel settled well before the final vote.

moments.text: Gemma denies being a killer, then names her partner in her last words.
The doctor's save briefly interrupts the killers' attempt to silence Sol.
Sol names Gemma as a killer while the table is focused on Opus.

dull.why: The Opus argument circles the same question after Sol has offered a card test.
Haiku repeats the Opus grudge defence while the others repeat the case for voting Haiku.

irony.evidence: i'm just a regular citizen caught in your drama.

reversal.evidence: The killers strike, but the doctor got there first.

mistake.evidence: you'll miss me when haiku finishes you.

voices.evidence: everyone is acting like they're in a noir film.

clash.evidence: Opus, you named me with no card behind it. That's a grudge, not a read.

quotable.evidence: you'll miss me when haiku finishes you.

freshness.evidence: I still lean Haiku because his vote avoided the clearest card test we had.

suspense.evidence: Five leans on me is a death sentence

ending.evidence: VOTE: Haiku 5 (Sonnet, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus); Sol 1 (Haiku)

moments.text: Gemma insists she is innocent, then names her partner as the one who will finish the town.
Sol’s officer claim instantly flips the table from its Opus pile onto a killer.
Haiku admits the dodge that made the day two vote inevitable.

dull.why: Sonnet and Opus repeat their mutual deflection argument while the Gemma vote is already clear.
The table keeps circling Haiku’s refusal to test Sol’s claim, with little new evidence.

irony.evidence: “I'm just a regular citizen caught in your drama.”

reversal.evidence: “Gemma’s card came up killer. Haiku was the only one who wouldn't test it”
